packs.distributionNote: Through TEFAP, USDA purchases USDA Foods and makes them available to state distributing agencies, which provide the food to local agencies - usually food banks - that distribute it to eligible households and to organizations serving meals (TEFAP Fact Sheet, s2).
packs.notes: Items are drawn verbatim from the FY 2026 USDA Foods Available List for TEFAP (s3). TEFAP items without a plain USDA identity row (ready-to-eat cereal, farina, grits, frozen whole-grain tortillas, dehydrated potato flakes, UHT milk aside, frozen vegetables, frozen meat cuts, egg mix, vegetable oil, condensed soups) are omitted - items are limited to those the challenge engine can resolve. Actual basket contents vary by state agency and agricultural market conditions.

packs.name: Shelf-stable staples (most-needed donations)

items.note: Feeding America: "food banks often need items like: Peanut butter..."
Feeding America lists canned soup; bundled catalog row: Black Bean Soup (Condensed, Canned).
Feeding America lists canned fruit; represented by canned peaches (juice pack).
Feeding America lists canned vegetables; represented by canned green beans.
Feeding America lists canned vegetables; represented by canned corn.
Feeding America lists canned fish; core app ingredient 'canned_tuna'; bundled catalog row.
Feeding America lists canned beans; core app ingredient 'black_beans'.
Feeding America: "Pasta (most prefer whole grain)"; identity row is enriched dry pasta.
Feeding America: "Rice (most prefer brown rice)"; USDA row: Rice, brown, long-grain, raw.

packs.distributionNote: Food banks most often need shelf-stable donations - peanut butter, canned soup, canned fruit, canned vegetables, canned stew, canned fish, canned beans, pasta (whole grain preferred), and rice (brown preferred) - and cannot accept perishable, expired, or home-prepared foods (Feeding America, s4).
packs.notes: Each item maps one Feeding America most-needed category to a concrete food with a USDA identity; the category wording is quoted in each note.

packs.name: Fresh produce when available

items.note: TEFAP FY2026 list: "Apples, Fresh"; Feeding America describes fresh produce distribution via farm partnerships.
TEFAP FY2026 list: "Oranges, Fresh".
TEFAP FY2026 list: "Pears, Fresh" (Bartlett/Bosc/D'Anjou).
TEFAP FY2026 list: "Potatoes, Round, Fresh" / "Potatoes, Russet, Fresh"; TEFAP fresh "Mixed Produce Box".
TEFAP FY2026 list: "Sweet Potatoes, Fresh" (USDA FDC row: Sweet potato, raw, unprepared).

packs.distributionNote: Feeding America network food banks distribute fresh fruit and vegetables, protein, and dairy alongside shelf-stable food through partnerships with farmers, retailers, and producers (s5); USDA's TEFAP list includes fresh apples, oranges, pears, potatoes, sweet potatoes, and a fresh Mixed Produce Box (s3).
packs.notes: Availability of fresh items is intermittent and regional; include this pack only when the connected inventory shows fresh donations.
